title: ViewSonic vCast Flaws Let Unauthenticated Attackers Gain Full Control of Smartboards
content_md: ViewSonic ViewBoard smart displays are exposed to a chain of critical vulnerabilities in the bundled vCast wireless sharing suite that could allow unauthenticated attackers on the same network to steal screen content, install malicious applications, and ultimately take full control of affected devices. CERT Coordination Center (CERT/CC) disclosed the issues in Vulnerability on September 24, warning that the flaws affect vCast-enabled ViewBoards deployed across enterprise and educational environments. The vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-82987, CVE-2026-82988, and CVE-2026-82989. ViewBoard devices are Android-based interactive displays commonly used in classrooms, meeting rooms, training facilities, and corporate collaboration spaces. ViewSonic vCast Flaws Their vCast software allows wireless connectivity and screen sharing between the display and devices running a compatible client application. However, researchers found that several network-accessible vCast endpoints do not require authentication, creating a path for nearby or internal attackers to compromise a smartboard without user interaction. The first flaw, CVE-2026-82989, affects vCast’s media streaming service. An attacker can send GET requests to exposed /snapshot or /screen API endpoints and retrieve JPEG images of the content currently displayed on the ViewBoard.
